tagline: A gold road north, and opals at the end of it.
intro: From the Y on County Road A-2 the loop runs southwest over rolling desert and lava hills, where cattle and wild game share the grazing in spring and fall, crosses the railroad into Dubois and turns north on Old Highway 91. The old road follows Beaver Creek on the line of an early trail to the Montana gold mines.
At Spencer the gold trail turns into an opal trail. From there the Spencer-Idmon road heads east on an old Nez Perce trail to meet the Fort Henry byway at Idmon, a pioneer town that no longer exists.

moments.title: Dubois
moments.text: Drought moved the railroad's water stop to Dry Creek, now Dubois, in 1892, and the town's first church, a Gothic Revival Episcopal church of 1905, now holds the Heritage Hall Museum.

moments.title: China Point
moments.text: By the story told here, a stage stalled in a blizzard south of Spencer, and its passengers, Chinese men bound to cook in the Montana mine camps, would not leave it and froze.

moments.title: Spencer
moments.text: Spencer is called the Opal Capital of America. A deer hunter found the opal in old volcanic rock in 1948, and the mines lie five or six miles out of town.

practical: County Road A-2 and the Spencer-Idmon road close in winter and become snowmobile trails.
